Misconfigurations.Title: IAM policies should not be granted directly to users.
Misconfigurations.Description: CIS recommends that you apply IAM policies directly to groups and roles but not users. Assigning privileges at the group or role level reduces the complexity of access management as the number of users grow. Reducing access management complexity might in turn reduce opportunity for a principal to inadvertently receive or retain excessive privileges.
Misconfigurations.Message: One or more policies are attached directly to a user
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Grant policies at the group level instead.

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Pass Role Filtering
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures any IAM pass role attached to roles are flagged and warned.
Misconfigurations.Message: IAM policy allows 'iam:PassRole' action
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Resolve permission escalations by denying pass role'

Misconfigurations.Title: Disallow unrestricted S3 IAM Policies
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensure that the creation of the unrestricted S3 IAM policies is disallowed.
Misconfigurations.Message: IAM policy allows 's3:*' action
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create more restrictive S3 policies

Misconfigurations.Title: Disallow unrestricted S3 IAM Policies
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensure that the creation of the unrestricted S3 IAM policies is disallowed.
Misconfigurations.Message: IAM role uses a policy that allows 's3:*' action
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create more restrictive S3 policies

Misconfigurations.Title: ECR repository policy must block public access
Misconfigurations.Description: Allowing public access to the ECR repository risks leaking sensitive of abusable information
Misconfigurations.Message: Policy provides public access to the ECR repository.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Do not allow public access in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM groups should have MFA enforcement activated.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM groups should be protected with multi factor authentication to add safe guards to password compromise.
Misconfigurations.Message: Multi-Factor authentication is not enforced for group
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use terraform-module/enforce-mfa/aws to ensure that MFA is enforced

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: SNS topic not encrypted with CMK.
Misconfigurations.Description: Topics should be encrypted with customer managed KMS keys and not default AWS managed keys, in order to allow granular key management.
Misconfigurations.Message: Topic encryption does not use a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use a CMK for SNS Topic encryption

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your S3 buckets. To gain greater control over encryption, such as key rotation, access policies, and auditability, use customer managed keys (CMKs) with SSE-KMS.
Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)

Misconfigurations.Title: A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
Misconfigurations.Message: Security group rule allows unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive cidr range

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudFront distribution allows unencrypted (HTTP) communications.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Plain HTTP is unencrypted and human-readable. This means that if a malicious actor was to eavesdrop on your connection, they would be able to see all of your data flowing back and forth.
You should use HTTPS, which is HTTP over an encrypted (TLS) connection, meaning eavesdroppers cannot read your traffic.
Misconfigurations.Message: Distribution allows unencrypted communications.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Only allow HTTPS for CloudFront distribution communication

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudFront distribution uses outdated SSL/TLS protocols.
Misconfigurations.Description:
You should not use outdated/insecure TLS versions for encryption. You should be using the latest TLS policies available.
Note: that setting *minimum_protocol_version = "TLSv1.X"* is only possible when *cloudfront_default_certificate* is false (eg. you are not using the cloudfront.net domain name).
If *cloudfront_default_certificate* is true then the Cloudfront API will only allow setting *minimum_protocol_version = "TLSv1"*, and setting it to any other value will result in a perpetual diff in your *terraform plan*'s.
The only option when using the cloudfront.net domain name is to ignore this rule.
Misconfigurations.Message: Distribution uses an insecure minimum TLS protocol version.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use the most modern TLS/SSL policies available

Misconfigurations.Title: Load balancer is exposed to the internet.
Misconfigurations.Description: There are many scenarios in which you would want to expose a load balancer to the wider internet, but this check exists as a warning to prevent accidental exposure of internal assets. You should ensure that this resource should be exposed publicly.
Misconfigurations.Message: Load balancer is exposed publicly.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Switch to an internal load balancer or add a tfsec ignore

Misconfigurations.Title: Redshift clusters should use at rest encryption
Misconfigurations.Description: Redshift clusters that contain sensitive data or are subject to regulation should be encrypted at rest to prevent data leakage should the infrastructure be compromised.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not use a customer managed encryption key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption using CMK

Misconfigurations.Title: Redshift cluster should be deployed into a specific VPC
Misconfigurations.Description:
Redshift clusters that are created without subnet details will be created in EC2 classic mode, meaning that they will be outside of a known VPC and running in tenant.
In order to benefit from the additional security features achieved with using an owned VPC, the subnet should be set.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster is deployed outside of a VPC.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Deploy Redshift cluster into a non default VPC

Misconfigurations.Title: Enable in-transit encryption for EMR clusters.
Misconfigurations.Description: Data stored within an EMR cluster should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is kept private.
Misconfigurations.Message: EMR cluster does not have in-transit encryption enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable in-transit encryption for EMR cluster

Misconfigurations.Title: Elasticsearch domain endpoint is using outdated TLS policy.
Misconfigurations.Description: You should not use outdated/insecure TLS versions for encryption. You should be using TLS v1.2+.
Misconfigurations.Message: Domain does not have a secure TLS policy.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use the most modern TLS/SSL policies available

Misconfigurations.Title: Neptune storage must be encrypted at rest
Misconfigurations.Description: Encryption of Neptune storage ensures that if their is compromise of the disks, the data is still protected.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not have storage encryption enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption of Neptune storage

Misconfigurations.Title: Neptune encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your Neptune underlying storage. To increase control of the encryption and manage factors like rotation use customer managed keys.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption using customer managed keys

Misconfigurations.Title: There is no encryption specified or encryption is disabled on the RDS Cluster.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption should be enabled for an RDS Aurora cluster.
When enabling encryption by setting the kms_key_id, the storage_encrypted must also be set to true.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not have storage encryption enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption for RDS clusters

Misconfigurations.Title: There is no encryption specified or encryption is disabled on the RDS Cluster.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption should be enabled for an RDS Aurora cluster.
When enabling encryption by setting the kms_key_id, the storage_encrypted must also be set to true.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not specify a customer managed key for storage encryption.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption for RDS clusters

Misconfigurations.Title: CodeBuild Project artifacts encryption should not be disabled
Misconfigurations.Description: All artifacts produced by your CodeBuild project pipeline should always be encrypted
Misconfigurations.Message: Encryption is not enabled for project artifacts.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption for CodeBuild project artifacts

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudTrail should use Customer managed keys to encrypt the logs
Misconfigurations.Description: Using AWS managed keys does not allow for fine grained control.  Using Customer managed keys provides comprehensive control over cryptographic keys, enabling management of policies, permissions, and rotation, thus enhancing security and compliance measures for sensitive data and systems.
Misconfigurations.Message: CloudTrail does not use a customer managed key to encrypt the logs.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use Customer managed key

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudTrail logs should be stored in S3 and also sent to CloudWatch Logs
Misconfigurations.Description:
Realtime log analysis is not available without enabling CloudWatch logging.

CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls made in a given account. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service.

CloudTrail uses Amazon S3 for log file storage and delivery, so log files are stored durably. In addition to capturing CloudTrail logs in a specified Amazon S3 bucket for long-term analysis, you can perform real-time analysis by configuring CloudTrail to send logs to CloudWatch Logs.

For a trail that is enabled in all Regions in an account, CloudTrail sends log files from all those Regions to a CloudWatch Logs log group.
Misconfigurations.Message: Trail does not have CloudWatch logging configured
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging to CloudWatch

Misconfigurations.Title: VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet "Rejects" for VPCs.
Misconfigurations.Description: VPC Flow Logs provide visibility into network traffic that traverses the VPC and can be used to detect anomalous traffic or insight during security workflows.
Misconfigurations.Message: VPC does not have VPC Flow Logs enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable flow logs for VPC

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS Clusters should have cluster control plane logging turned on
Misconfigurations.Description: By default cluster control plane logging is not turned on. Logging is available for audit, api, authenticator, controllerManager and scheduler. All logging should be turned on for cluster control plane.
Misconfigurations.Message: Control plane API logging is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for the EKS control plane

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS Clusters should have cluster control plane logging turned on
Misconfigurations.Description: By default cluster control plane logging is not turned on. Logging is available for audit, api, authenticator, controllerManager and scheduler. All logging should be turned on for cluster control plane.
Misconfigurations.Message: Control plane audit logging is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for the EKS control plane

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS Clusters should have cluster control plane logging turned on

Misconfigurations.Description: API Gateway stages should have access log settings block configured to track all access to a particular stage. This should be applied to both v1 and v2 gateway stages.
Misconfigurations.Message: Access logging is not configured.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for API Gateway stages

Misconfigurations.Description: X-Ray tracing enables end-to-end debugging and analysis of all API Gateway HTTP requests.
Misconfigurations.Message: X-Ray tracing is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable tracing

Misconfigurations.Title: ECS clusters should have container insights enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Cloudwatch Container Insights provide more metrics and logs for container based applications and micro services.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not have container insights enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Container Insights

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Bucket Logging
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures S3 bucket logging is enabled for S3 buckets
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket has logging disabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging

Enabling Performance insights allows for greater depth in monitoring data.
For example, information about active sessions could help diagose a compromise or assist in the investigation
Misconfigurations.Message: Instance does not have performance insights enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable performance insights

Misconfigurations.Title: Neptune logs export should be enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Neptune does not have auditing by default. To ensure that you are able to accurately audit the usage of your Neptune instance you should enable export logs.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not have audit logging enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable export logs

Misconfigurations.Title: Neptune encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your Neptune underlying storage. To increase control of the encryption and manage factors like rotation use customer managed keys.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.

Misconfigurations.Title: DocumentDB logs export should be enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Document DB does not have auditing by default. To ensure that you are able to accurately audit the usage of your DocumentDB cluster you should enable export logs.
Misconfigurations.Message: Neither CloudWatch audit nor profiler log exports are enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable export logs

Misconfigurations.Title: DocumentDB encryption should use Customer Managed Keys

Misconfigurations.Title: AWS best practice to not use the default VPC for workflows
Misconfigurations.Description: Default VPC does not have a lot of the critical security features that standard VPC comes with, new resources should not be created in the default VPC and it should not be present in the Terraform.
Misconfigurations.Message: Default VPC is used.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create a non-default vpc for resources to be created in

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudFront distribution does not have a WAF in front.
Misconfigurations.Description: You should configure a Web Application Firewall in front of your CloudFront distribution. This will mitigate many types of attacks on your web application.
Misconfigurations.Message: Distribution does not utilize a WAF.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable WAF for the CloudFront distribution

Misconfigurations.Title: Security groups should not allow unrestricted ingress to SSH or RDP from any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Security groups provide stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS
resources. It is recommended that no security group allows unrestricted ingress access to
remote server administration ports, such as SSH to port 22 and RDP to port 3389.
Misconfigurations.Message: Security group rule allows unrestricted ingress from any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive CIDR range

Misconfigurations.Title: Security groups should not allow unrestricted ingress to SSH or RDP from any IP address.

Misconfigurations.Title: RDS Cluster and RDS instance should have backup retention longer than default 1 day
Misconfigurations.Description: RDS backup retention for clusters defaults to 1 day, this may not be enough to identify and respond to an issue. Backup retention periods should be set to a period that is a balance on cost and limiting risk.
Misconfigurations.Message: Instance has very low backup retention period.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Explicitly set the retention period to greater than the default

Misconfigurations.Description: Ensure IAM Database Authentication is enabled for RDS database instances to manage database access
Misconfigurations.Message: Instance does not have IAM Authentication enabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Modify the PostgreSQL and MySQL type RDS instances to enable IAM database authentication.

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should block public ACL
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should block public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By blocking, PUTs with fail if the object has any public ACL a.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public acls
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable blocking any PUT calls with a public ACL specified

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should block public policy
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 bucket policy should have block public policy to prevent users from putting a policy that enable public access.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public policies
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Prevent policies that allow public access being PUT

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Bucket Logging
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures S3 bucket logging is enabled for S3 buckets
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket has logging disabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Data should be versioned
Misconfigurations.Description:
Versioning in Amazon S3 is a means of keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket.

You can use the S3 Versioning feature to preserve, retrieve, and restore every version of every object stored in your buckets.

With versioning you can recover more easily from both unintended user actions and application failures.

When you enable versioning, also keep in mind the potential costs of storing noncurrent versions of objects. To help manage those costs, consider setting up an S3 Lifecycle configuration.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not have versioning enabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable versioning to protect against accidental/malicious removal or modification

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access Block should Ignore Public ACL
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should ignore public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By ignoring rather than blocking, PUT calls with public ACLs will still be applied but the ACL will be ignored.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public acls
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable ignoring the application of public ACLs in PUT calls

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Buckets not publicly accessible through ACL.
Misconfigurations.Description: Buckets should not have ACLs that allow public access
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket has a public ACL: "public-read"
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Don't use canned ACLs or switch to private acl

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should restrict public bucket to limit access
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should restrict public policies for the bucket. By enabling, the restrict_public_buckets, only the bucket owner and AWS Services can access if it has a public policy.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not restricting public buckets
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit the access to public buckets to only the owner or AWS Services (eg; CloudFront)

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 buckets should each define an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block
Misconfigurations.Description: The "block public access" settings in S3 override individual policies that apply to a given bucket, meaning that all public access can be controlled in one central types for that bucket. It is therefore good practice to define these settings for each bucket in order to clearly define the public access that can be allowed for it.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not have a corresponding public access block.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Define a aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for the given bucket to control public access policies

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys

Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)

Misconfigurations.Description: By enabling encryption on EBS volumes you protect the volume, the disk I/O and any derived snapshots from compromise if intercepted.
Misconfigurations.Message: EBS volume is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption of EBS volumes

Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should block public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By blocking, PUTs with fail if the object has any public ACL a.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public acls
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable blocking any PUT calls with a public ACL specified

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should block public policy
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 bucket policy should have block public policy to prevent users from putting a policy that enable public access.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public policies
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Prevent policies that allow public access being PUT

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Bucket Logging

Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Data should be versioned
Misconfigurations.Description:
Versioning in Amazon S3 is a means of keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket.

You can use the S3 Versioning feature to preserve, retrieve, and restore every version of every object stored in your buckets.

With versioning you can recover more easily from both unintended user actions and application failures.

When you enable versioning, also keep in mind the potential costs of storing noncurrent versions of objects. To help manage those costs, consider setting up an S3 Lifecycle configuration.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not have versioning enabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable versioning to protect against accidental/malicious removal or modification

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access Block should Ignore Public ACL
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should ignore public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By ignoring rather than blocking, PUT calls with public ACLs will still be applied but the ACL will be ignored.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not blocking public acls
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable ignoring the application of public ACLs in PUT calls

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Buckets not publicly accessible through ACL.
Misconfigurations.Description: Buckets should not have ACLs that allow public access
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket has a public ACL: "public-read"
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Don't use canned ACLs or switch to private acl

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should restrict public bucket to limit access
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should restrict public policies for the bucket. By enabling, the restrict_public_buckets, only the bucket owner and AWS Services can access if it has a public policy.
Misconfigurations.Message: No public access block so not restricting public buckets
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit the access to public buckets to only the owner or AWS Services (eg; CloudFront)

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 buckets should each define an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block
Misconfigurations.Description: The "block public access" settings in S3 override individual policies that apply to a given bucket, meaning that all public access can be controlled in one central types for that bucket. It is therefore good practice to define these settings for each bucket in order to clearly define the public access that can be allowed for it.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not have a corresponding public access block.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Define a aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for the given bucket to control public access policies

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your S3 buckets. To gain greater control over encryption, such as key rotation, access policies, and auditability, use customer managed keys (CMKs) with SSE-KMS.
Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudTrail logs should be stored in S3 and also sent to CloudWatch Logs
Misconfigurations.Description:
Realtime log analysis is not available without enabling CloudWatch logging.

CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls made in a given account. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service.

CloudTrail uses Amazon S3 for log file storage and delivery, so log files are stored durably. In addition to capturing CloudTrail logs in a specified Amazon S3 bucket for long-term analysis, you can perform real-time analysis by configuring CloudTrail to send logs to CloudWatch Logs.

For a trail that is enabled in all Regions in an account, CloudTrail sends log files from all those Regions to a CloudWatch Logs log group.
Misconfigurations.Message: Trail does not have CloudWatch logging configured
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging to CloudWatch
